original_title: Sample: Larnaca seafront upgrade enters final phase
rewritten_title: Larnaca's Seafront Makeover Nears the Finish Line
summary: The final phase of the Larnaca seafront upgrade is under way, with wider pavements, new lighting and extra green space planned along the promenade.
full_article:
Work on the last stretch of the Larnaca seafront has begun, marking the final phase of a project that has reshaped the town's most visited promenade. Crews are laying new paving, replacing street lighting and planting additional trees along the walkway.

The upgrade is designed to give more room to pedestrians and cyclists while keeping access open for the cafes and shops that line the front. Temporary diversions are in place, and businesses have been told that works will be staged to limit disruption during busy hours.

Shop owners say the months of construction have been difficult, but many expect the finished promenade to draw more visitors outside the summer season. The remaining works are scheduled in sections so that parts of the seafront reopen as soon as they are complete.

original_title: Sample: Solar capacity grows as households add rooftop panels
rewritten_title: Rooftop Solar Boom Pushes Cyprus Toward a Greener Grid
summary: More households are installing rooftop solar panels, adding pressure on the grid to store and manage daytime surplus power.
full_article:
Rooftop solar installations continue to spread across the island as households look for ways to cut their electricity bills. Installers report full order books, with waiting times stretching to several weeks in some districts.

The growth brings a new challenge. On bright days the system produces more power than it can use around midday, while demand peaks after sunset when panels are idle. Engineers say storage, both at home and at grid scale, is the missing piece.

Homeowners considering a system are advised to compare quotes, check the warranty on inverters and panels, and ask how a battery could be added later. For many families the payback period remains attractive even without storage.

original_title: Sample: Hotels report strong autumn bookings
rewritten_title: Autumn Sun Keeps Cyprus Hotels Busy Well Past Summer
summary: Hoteliers report healthy autumn occupancy as visitors take advantage of warm weather and quieter beaches.
full_article:
Hotels in the coastal resorts are reporting a busy autumn, with warm sea temperatures and calmer beaches tempting visitors long after the peak months have passed. Many properties that once closed in October now plan to stay open into the winter.

The shift reflects a wider effort to spread tourism across the year. Walking routes, wine villages and cycling holidays are being promoted alongside the traditional sun and sea offer, bringing guests to inland areas that see little summer trade.

Staffing remains the main concern for operators. Longer seasons mean more stable jobs, but hoteliers say recruiting and keeping trained workers is harder than filling rooms.

Passenger numbers will be reviewed after the first months of operation. Planners say that routes which prove popular could gain extra departures, while quieter ones may be adjusted.

original_title: Sample: Reservoir levels remain low ahead of winter
rewritten_title: Low Reservoirs Leave Cyprus Hoping for a Wet Winter
summary: Reservoir levels are well below capacity at the start of the rainy season, renewing calls to save water.
full_article:
The island's reservoirs are entering the rainy season with stocks well below capacity, a familiar worry after a long, dry summer. Water managers are watching the first autumn storms closely.

Desalination covers much of the drinking water supply in the towns, but farming still depends heavily on stored rainfall. Growers say that another dry winter would force difficult choices about which crops to plant.

Households are being reminded of simple steps that add up: fixing leaks, watering gardens in the evening and reusing grey water where possible. Long term, wider use of recycled water for irrigation is seen as essential.

Farmers welcomed the rain but said far more is needed. The coming weeks are expected to stay changeable, with sunny spells between showers.
